'''''Curio repens''''' (syn. ''Senecio serpens'') is a [[species]] of [[succulent]] [[groundcover]] plant in the [[genus]] ''[[Curio (plant)|Curio]]'', in the [[Asteraceae]] family. Commonly named '''blue chalksticks''', '''blue chalk fingers''' and also '''snake ragwort''',<ref>{{cite web |title=Curio repens |url=https://apps.cals.arizona.edu/arboretum/taxon.aspx?id=1164 |work=[[The University of Arizona]] |publisher=[[Arizona Board of Regents]] |accessdate=21 July 2024}}</ref> it is frequently used in [[Mediterranean climate]] landscaping and as an [[ornamental plant]]. Its native range is the [[Cape Province]] of [[South Africa]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Curio repens (L.) P.V.Heath |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:997629-1 |work=Plants of the World Online |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] |accessdate=4 May 2026}}</ref>

==Description==
It is a semi-trailing, low-growing dwarf [[shrub]] that forms a dense mat that reaches only about 20 cm (8 in) in height and features silvery-blueish, finger-like fleshy leaves.<ref name="afpd"/> It produces small and round, pompom-like flowers that may superficially resemble a [[virus]]. The flowers appear as [[Ivory (color)|off-white]] from distance, but would have yellow and pink tinges on the [[stamen]] up-close. Flowering season is usually between spring and autumn. It was first formally described as ''Cacalia repens'' by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1767.<ref name="IPNI"/>

It should be distinguished from ''[[Curio talinoides]]'' by its shorter, broader and often boat-shaped leaves.<ref>[http://pza.sanbi.org/curio-talinoides Curio talinoides (DC.) P.V.Heath] by PlantZAfrica.com</ref>

==Cultivation==
Drought tolerant, the plant is used as a [[ground cover]], border plant or in a [[rock garden]]. It is grown in [[sand]]y, dry to slightly moist soils in sun or some partial shade. It is easily propagated by [[cuttings (plants)|cuttings]]. Visually-similar to the [[Aizoaceae|ice plant]]s of ''[[Mesembryanthemum]]'', ''C. repens'' is typically found growing in and among rocky crevices and exposed ledges on dry, rubble-strewn [[sandstone]] slopes, where drainage is swift and sun exposure and airflow is high.

There is a [[Hybrid (biology)|hybrid]] of this and ''[[Curio talinoides]]'' that is known as [[× Curio 'Trident Blue'|'Trident Blue']].
